rationale.coverholder_background:
· The MGA is a subsidiary of Beazley Holdings, Inc and is overseen by a board of Beazley staff chaired by TBC to which Simon Richardson reports – Richard Montminy is also on the board. 
· Seed funding is provided by Beazley and can be drawn down to meet all BHI Digital’s opex (salaries, technology, office space, travel and entertainment etc.)  
· BHI Digital, LLC is incorporated in the State of Delaware. 
· Underwriting operation will now be in Miami having moved from Chicago in December 2022. 
· BHI Digital is a fully empowered end to end product owner. 
· BHI is served by a small product and tech team with which they co-create, allowing analysis on whether the platform and UW product is feasible (possible, affordable, maintainable). 
· They will provide real time data, control and reporting, follow form for claims that reduces LAE. 
· The launch product (Wind Deductible Buybacks) has been approved with Property Risks and went live in 2020. 
· Quake Deductible Buybacks were approved in November 2020 and are now being quoted on the platform. 
· Full value quake was approved in August 2023.

rationale.rc_commentary:
As a result we expect to see a risk adjusted rate reduction of between 4.5% and 5% across the whole of the Section A portfolio in 2025. As a reminder, we had expected rates to remain flat with potential for 2.5% rate increase under Section A due to storm zone loads.
The combination of a lower than anticipated coastal demand for wind deductible buybacks and the sharp deterioration in rating environment in coastal areas has driven this swing.
A 5% risk adjusted rate reduction is envisaged for 2026 for Section A, and 7.5% for Section B.

rationale.uw_commentary:
Market conditions within the 2025 E&S property sector have unfolded largely in accordance with prior forecasts over the course of this year, confirming earlier expectations of softening terms and heightened complexity for BHI Digital in income projection.
The portfolio continues to demonstrate excellent balance at an aggregate level, but growing into this market is increasingly challenging when applying our aggregate controls and algorithmic rating methodology.
Whilst current premium income is tracking below our plan for 20% growth, the growth projection for the year of 15% for Section A (Property) of the binding authority remains an excellent result considering market conditions.

Consistent with our application of a 20% expense allocation to Beazley Syndicates we will amend Appendix 1 of the binding authority agreement to apply a 20% expense outgo calculated against gross premium written, less all commissions including those of the binding authority intermediary.
